processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10×5×2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
Solution-treated samples aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h, followed by water quenching; this sample is the 17Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 6 h.

structures.overall_structure: After aging the 17Al alloy at 650 °C for 6 h, the α (BCC) matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn, with fine new BCC and FCC (Cu-rich) precipitates distributed within the β-Mn. At temperatures of 600 °C and above the α → β-Mn transformation of the 17Al alloy is essentially complete within ~1 h of aging.

phases_present.morphology: near-equiaxed grains resulting from the near-complete α→β-Mn transformation
fine precipitates within/v at the interfaces between β-Mn
fine particles distributed at the β-Mn interfaces, frequently containing FCC twins

precipitates.distribution: within the β-Mn / at β-Mn interfaces

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: The fine BCC and FCC Cu-rich phases form at the β-Mn interfaces. The BCC phase is attributed to enrichment of the BCC-stabilizing element Al around the β-Mn interfaces, while the Cu-rich phase forms due to the limited solubility of Cu in Fe-based alloys and the expulsion of Cu from β-Mn during its precipitation and growth.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured at a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the samples after different aging treatments
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 17Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 6 h had a Vickers hardness of 838.3 ± 20.7 HV; the 650 °C series stays nearly time-independent (828.4–838.3 HV over 1–10 h).

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase compositions of the alloys after selected aging treatments
characterization_methods.key_findings: After the selected aging treatments the alloys contain α/D0₃ together with both α-Mn and β-Mn, indicating the two Mn-rich phases co-precipitated before the α matrix fully transformed to β-Mn.

characterization_methods.technique: Secondary-electron (SE) SEM imaging and EDS analysis
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SE imaging and EDS at 5 kV
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases such as α-Mn and β-Mn in the aged samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: The SE images reveal the α→β-Mn transformation and fine new precipitates; the 17Al alloy matrix is essentially transformed at 550 °C by 6–10 h and within 1 h at 600 °C and above.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the microstructural origin of the rapid aging hardening (phase mapping/IPF)
characterization_methods.key_findings: EBSD shows the α→β-Mn transformation and the appearance of new BCC and FCC precipitates within β-Mn at higher aging temperatures.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Talos F200X microscope equipped with an EDS detector, operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 200 kV; ion-thinned foils ~90 μm ground then punched to 3 mm diameter
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate the microstructure of the ultra-high hardness alloys (β-Mn, FCC Cu-rich phase and twins)
characterization_methods.key_findings: TEM confirms the FCC Cu-rich phase (with FCC twins) at β-Mn interfaces and identifies β-Mn by SAED/HRTEM.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: indentation depth 200 nm; test points spaced ≥5 μm apart; samples mechanically polished
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the intrinsic micro-hardness of β-Mn and of the precipitate phases in the hardest samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: The intrinsic hardness of β-Mn in the hardest 17Al sample was 12.2 ± 0.1 GPa; the overall nanoindentation hardness decreased with increasing Al content.

unmapped_findings: For the 17Al alloy, the Vickers hardness at 650 °C aging is essentially time-independent across 1–10 h (828.4 ± 26.6, 834.2 ± 14.0, 838.3 ± 20.7 and 833.2 ± 18.7 HV for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h respectively), so the 650 °C/6 h sample (838.3 ± 20.7 HV) is representative of the 650 °C plateau.

Although most β-Mn/precipitate characterization (EBSD Fig. 5, TEM Fig. 12, nanoindentation and fracture toughness) of the 17Al alloy was performed on the 575 °C/6 h hardest sample rather than this 650 °C/6 h sample, the general statement that at temperatures of 600 °C and above the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn within 1 h and that numerous fine BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates form within the β-Mn applies to this 650 °C/6 h sample.
The 17Al alloy solution-treated baseline hardness was 259.8 ± 1.5 HV (Table 3), which applies to the parent state of this sample before aging at 650 °C for 6 h.
